generic: Calamine (Calamine topical / zinc oxide with ferric oxide)
quick: Apply to affected skin as needed, up to 3-4 times daily (shake well before use)
Considered low risk; negligible systemic absorption from intact skin
Low risk; avoid applying to the nipple/areola if breastfeeding
Local skin response; resolution of itching/irritation
summary: Calamine lotion is an over-the-counter topical preparation of zinc oxide with a small amount of ferric (iron) oxide (giving its pink color). It acts as a mild astringent, skin protectant, and antipruritic to relieve itching, pain, and discomfort from minor skin irritations such as poison ivy/oak/sumac, insect bites, and minor rashes. It is for external use only, has negligible systemic absorption, and is generally very well tolerated.
indications: Relief of itching and discomfort from poison ivy, poison oak, and poison sumac
Relief of itching from insect bites and stings
Soothing of minor skin irritations, minor rashes, and minor skin abrasions
Drying of oozing and weeping due to these conditions

dosage.c: Minor skin irritation / itch (poison ivy, bites, rash)
dosage.d: Apply to the affected area as needed; shake well before use
dosage.t: As needed, up to 3-4 times daily

admin: Shake the lotion well before each application
Apply to clean, dry affected skin and allow to dry; reapply as needed
Avoid the eyes and do not apply to large open wounds or broken skin
moa: Calamine is a combination of zinc oxide with a small proportion of ferric oxide. Applied topically it acts as a mild astringent that helps dry weeping or oozing lesions, and as a protectant that forms a soothing layer over irritated skin. The cooling, drying effect relieves itching and minor pain. Its action is local; there is essentially no systemic absorption through intact skin.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to calamine or formulation components
relative: Application to deep or puncture wounds, serious burns, or large areas of broken skin
Use near or in the eyes

preg: Calamine is applied topically with negligible systemic absorption and is considered low risk in pregnancy when used as directed.
lact: Calamine is considered low risk during breastfeeding owing to negligible systemic absorption; avoid applying to the nipple or areola, or wash the area before nursing.
renal: No dose adjustment is needed; systemic absorption from topical use is negligible.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is needed; systemic absorption from topical use is negligible.

minor: Other topical products on the same area (may alter drying effect or tolerability)

emergency: Signs of a severe allergic reaction (widespread rash, swelling, difficulty breathing) - very rare

monitoring: Resolution of itching and skin irritation
Any increase in redness, swelling, or new rash at the site
Need to consult a doctor if the condition worsens or persists beyond 7 days
counsel: For external use only - keep away from the eyes
Shake well before applying and let it dry on the skin
Stop use and ask a doctor if the condition worsens, symptoms last more than 7 days, or clear up and recur
Do not apply to deep wounds, serious burns, or large areas of broken skin
Keep out of reach of children; if swallowed, contact a Poison Control Center
pk: Soothing/cooling relief shortly after application as the lotion dries
Local effect only; no meaningful systemic peak
Effect lasts while the dried film remains; reapply as needed
Store at room temperature; do not freeze; shake before use
pearls: Active ingredients are zinc oxide plus a small amount of ferric oxide (which gives the characteristic pink color)
A classic, well-tolerated remedy for itch from poison ivy, insect bites, and minor rashes
Works locally as a drying astringent and protectant - essentially no systemic absorption
It relieves symptoms but does not treat the underlying cause (e.g. it does not neutralize urushiol once dermatitis is established)
OTC product - not an FDA new-drug-approved single entity; regulated under the OTC skin protectant/antipruritic monograph
missed: Calamine is applied as needed for symptom relief, so there is no fixed schedule and no missed dose. Reapply when itching or irritation returns, as directed.
overdose: Topical overdose is not a meaningful risk. If swallowed, contact a Poison Control Center; ingestion may cause mild gastrointestinal upset. Excessive application may cause local dryness - wipe off excess.
